title: Exodus Bible Quiz - Chapter 5
description: Ten questions on Exodus 5: Pharaoh's refusal, bricks without straw and the complaint of Israel's officers.

questions.text: Why did Moses and Aaron say Yahweh wanted Pharaoh to let his people go?
questions.explanation: They told Pharaoh that Yahweh says, "Let my people go, that they may hold a feast to me in the wilderness."

answers.text: To hold a feast to him in the wilderness
To return to the land of Canaan
To rest from their work for one month
To build an altar in Goshen

questions.text: How did Pharaoh answer the request?
questions.explanation: Pharaoh said, "Who is Yahweh, that I should listen to his voice to let Israel go? I don't know Yahweh."

answers.text: "Your God is welcome in my land."
"Who is Yahweh, that I should listen to his voice?"

questions.text: How far into the wilderness did Moses and Aaron ask to go?
questions.explanation: They asked, "Please let us go three days' journey into the wilderness, and sacrifice to Yahweh, our God."

questions.text: What did Pharaoh command the taskmasters to stop giving the people?
questions.explanation: Pharaoh commanded, "You shall no longer give the people straw to make brick, as before."

questions.text: What did Pharaoh require concerning the number of bricks the people made?
questions.explanation: Pharaoh said the taskmasters must require the number of bricks they made before, without diminishing anything.

questions.text: What did the people gather throughout Egypt in place of straw?
questions.explanation: The people were scattered throughout all the land of Egypt to gather stubble for straw.

questions.text: Who were beaten when the brick quota was not met?
questions.explanation: The officers of the children of Israel, whom Pharaoh's taskmasters had set over them, were beaten.

questions.text: What did Pharaoh call the Israelites when their officers complained?
questions.explanation: Pharaoh said, "You are idle! You are idle! Therefore you say, 'Let's go and sacrifice to Yahweh.'"

questions.text: What did the officers say Moses and Aaron had made them in Pharaoh's eyes?
questions.explanation: The officers said Moses and Aaron had made them "a stench to be abhorred" in the eyes of Pharaoh and his servants.

questions.text: What did Moses say to Yahweh at the end of the chapter?
questions.explanation: Moses asked, "Lord, why have you brought trouble on this people? Why is it that you have sent me?"

answers.text: "Why is it that you have sent me?"
"I will speak to Pharaoh once more."
